reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Laparoscopic adrenalectomy for a well prepared noradrenergic pheochromocytoma (14 days phenoxybenzamine, then metoprolol, meets targets). The challenge is intraop management: surges with induction, insufflation and tumor handling, then hypotension and hypoglycemia after vein ligation.

asa.rationale: Catecholamine secreting tumor with LVH and secondary hypertension.

decision.rationale: Meets Roizen style targets: seated BP under 130/80, standing SBP over 90, HR targets met, ST changes resolved, Hct fell with volume expansion, no paroxysms for a week.

redFlags.evidence: Pheo; 2019 lap chole SBP 220 on induction.
redFlags.implication: Hypertensive crisis, arrhythmia, ischemia with intubation, positioning, insufflation, tumor manipulation.
redFlags.action: Pre induction arterial line, deep induction, nitroprusside or nicardipine and esmolol ready, communicate with surgeon.

redFlags.implication: Profound hypotension from catecholamine withdrawal with residual alpha blockade.
redFlags.action: Stop vasodilators before clamp, fluids, phenylephrine or norepinephrine, vasopressin if refractory.
Avoid metoclopramide, droperidol, ephedrine, ketamine, histamine releasers (morphine, atracurium), desflurane surges.
Glucose checks intraop after ligation and hourly postop.

redFlags.evidence: Germline panel pending; aunt with adrenal tumor.
redFlags.action: MEN2 screen normal; note pending results.
Axillary roll, padding, check BP after positioning.

planItems.item: Arterial line before induction; two large bore IVs
Propofol, opioid, lidocaine; avoid ketamine and ephedrine
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision
SICU or step down with glucose monitoring

boothComplications.why: Differential for tachycardia and hypertension in pheochromocytoma
